generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `TypeError` from `torch.set_autocast_enabled`: `enabled` must be `bool`, not `str`, after `torch.cuda.amp.autocast("cuda")`; or failure after constructing `torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler("cuda")`.
repair_steps: Identify whether the imported context/scaler comes from `torch.cuda.amp` or `torch.amp`.
With `torch.cuda.amp.autocast`, do not pass `"cuda"` positionally; use the boolean `enabled` contract.
When supplying a device string, consistently use `torch.amp.autocast("cuda")` and `torch.amp.GradScaler("cuda")`.
Keep the CPU/non-CUDA path explicitly disabled instead of passing a device string to the legacy API.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The legacy CUDA AMP namespace interprets the first positional argument as an enable flag, while the modern AMP namespace accepts the device type; mixing the two contracts converts `"cuda"` into an invalid boolean argument.
generalized_repairs.title: Keep autocast and GradScaler namespace contracts consistent
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when AMP fails before the first backward pass and the traceback contains `set_autocast_enabled`, `enabled`, `GradScaler`, or a positional `"cuda"` argument.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `RuntimeError` or `_pickle.UnpicklingError` while loading a locally saved checkpoint under PyTorch 2.6; the checkpoint dictionary includes non-tensor values such as NumPy scalar validation scores.
repair_steps: Confirm the checkpoint was created by the same trusted pipeline.
Load that trusted checkpoint with `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)`.
Preserve the existing device mapping and then load the contained model state into the matching model definition.
Do not apply this option to an untrusted checkpoint.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: PyTorch 2.6 defaults `torch.load` to `weights_only=True`, whose restricted unpickler rejects NumPy scalars stored alongside the model state.
generalized_repairs.title: Load trusted mixed-content checkpoints explicitly under PyTorch 2.6
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use only when a trusted, locally generated checkpoint fails to unpickle after training and the error mentions the `weights_only` default.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `TypeError: ReduceLROnPlateau.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'verbose'` at scheduler construction.
repair_steps: Remove only the unsupported `verbose` keyword from `ReduceLROnPlateau`.
Retain supported operands such as `mode`, `factor`, and `patience`.
If learning-rate logging is needed, read it from the optimizer or scheduler state outside the constructor.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The installed PyTorch scheduler signature does not accept `verbose`, regardless of whether another PyTorch release did.
generalized_repairs.title: Remove unsupported ReduceLROnPlateau verbosity
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when model construction reaches `ReduceLROnPlateau` but training never starts because `verbose` is rejected.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `LGBMClassifier.fit()` rejects `verbose`, or native `lgb.train()` rejects `verbose_eval`.
repair_steps: For the sklearn wrapper, remove `verbose` from `.fit()` and control verbosity through supported constructor parameters or callbacks.
For native `lgb.train`, replace `verbose_eval` with a supported callback such as `lgb.log_evaluation(0)` when silence is required.
Keep early-stopping callbacks separate from logging callbacks.
Apply the branch matching the exact callable in the traceback.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The installed LightGBM version exposes verbosity through different interfaces for the sklearn wrapper and native training API; unsupported legacy keywords were passed to the wrong callable.
generalized_repairs.title: Route LightGBM verbosity through the supported interface
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when LightGBM stops at method dispatch with an unexpected `verbose` or `verbose_eval` keyword.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `XGBClassifier.fit()` rejects `early_stopping_rounds`; or full-data refitting raises `Must have at least 1 validation dataset for early stopping`.
repair_steps: For the affected sklearn wrapper, place `early_stopping_rounds` in `XGBClassifier(...)`, not in `.fit()`.
During fold training, supply the genuine validation partition through `eval_set`.
For a final full-data fit with no separate evaluation set, instantiate a model without early stopping rather than retaining the constructor setting.
Do not reuse the training data as a nominal validation set merely to satisfy the API.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Early stopping is estimator configuration in the installed wrapper and also requires an evaluation dataset; moving between fold training and full-data refitting without changing that configuration violates one of those contracts.
generalized_repairs.title: Configure XGBoost early stopping at construction and only with an eval set
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when the installed `XGBClassifier` rejects the fit keyword or when a final refit inherits early stopping but has no `eval_set`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `TypeError: Booster.predict() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ntree_limit'` after successful XGBoost training.
repair_steps: Read the trained booster’s `best_iteration`.
Replace `ntree_limit=best_iteration` with the supplied compatible form `iteration_range=(0, best_iteration)`.
Apply the same prediction contract to validation and test calls.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The installed XGBoost booster removed the legacy `ntree_limit` prediction keyword in favor of `iteration_range`.
generalized_repairs.title: Replace deprecated XGBoost ntree_limit prediction
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when boosting completes but post-training prediction alone fails on `ntree_limit`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Immediate `SyntaxError` or `IndentationError` from notebook magic (`!pip`), raw Markdown fences, replacement markers, bare prose, or unexpectedly indented model/training statements.
repair_steps: Remove notebook-only shell magic from standard `.py` files and provision dependencies outside Python source.
Remove raw Markdown fences, replacement directives, and un-commented explanatory prose.
Normalize each affected block so its indentation matches the enclosing function, class, or loop.
Perform a parse-only validation before starting data loading or training.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Non-Python artifacts or malformed block indentation were inserted into executable source, so the parser failed before runtime semantics could be evaluated.
generalized_repairs.title: Strip notebook and editing artifacts before executing generated scripts
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when execution stops at parsing and the offending line is not a valid Python statement.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `KeyError` for `margin_1`, `shape_1`, or `texture_1` when the CSV contains `margin1`, `shape1`, and `texture1`; or `IndexError` from sorting names with `x.split('_')[1]`.
repair_steps: Inspect the actual DataFrame columns before constructing feature lists.
Select the observed prefixes and parse trailing numeric suffixes without assuming an underscore.
Verify the same ordered feature columns exist in train and test.
Use `sample_submission.csv` columns excluding `id` as the final class-probability order.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The code hardcoded a different naming convention and suffix grammar from the supplied dataset, then propagated that assumption into selection, sorting, and submission construction.
generalized_repairs.title: Derive feature and class ordering from the actual files
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when column selection or natural sorting fails before preprocessing, especially for the leaf `margin`, `shape`, and `texture` families.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `NameError` for a variable, loader, function, constant, or alias that is defined later or under another name, including `X_train_fold` versus `X_train`, undefined loaders, `train_ids`, `batch_size`, or a default-argument constant.
repair_steps: Define constants used in default arguments before the function definition because defaults are evaluated immediately.
Define IDs, split indices, loaders, and transformed arrays before their first top-level call site.
Choose one canonical name for each artifact and replace stale aliases rather than defining duplicate near-equivalents.
Order helper function definitions before top-level calls that execute them.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Execution order or alias drift left the referenced symbol absent from the active scope at the moment Python evaluated it.
generalized_repairs.title: Resolve use-before-definition and stale aliases before training
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when a `NameError` identifies a symbol that visibly exists elsewhere in the file but only later, locally, or under a different name.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `UnboundLocalError` when `combined_features` is created only under `if fit_new:` but used for validation; or `NameError: self is not defined` when a standalone preprocessing function references `self.pca_objects`.
repair_steps: Compute input-derived arrays such as `combined_features` on every fit and transform call before conditional estimator logic.
Fit scalers or PCA objects only on the authorized training partition.
Return the fitted objects explicitly or pass them into later transform calls.
Do not reference `self` from a standalone function unless the function is made an actual bound method.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Required transform inputs or fitted state were hidden inside a branch or nonexistent object scope, so validation/test execution could not access them.
generalized_repairs.title: Carry fitted preprocessing state explicitly across fit and transform
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when training preprocessing works but the same function fails for validation or test because a branch-local variable or object state is unavailable.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A model `forward()` references an initializer-local dimension such as `tabular_dim` or creates `nn.Linear`/parameters dynamically behind `hasattr` checks.
repair_steps: Store required dimensions as instance attributes during `__init__`.
Construct projection, gate, and bias parameters in `__init__`, not on the first forward pass.
Use `forward()` only to apply already registered modules to tensors.
Recreate the optimizer after correcting module construction so every trainable parameter is registered.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Initializer-local symbols do not exist in `forward`, and layers created dynamically after optimizer construction are not reliably registered or optimized.
generalized_repairs.title: Register all trainable layers and parameters in __init__
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when the first forward pass raises a dimension-variable `NameError` or when the model conditionally creates trainable objects during `forward()`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `state_dict` loading reports spectral-normalization keys such as `_orig`, `_u`, `_v` versus plain `in_proj_weight`, or reports an `AveragedModel` `module.` prefix mismatch.
repair_steps: Instantiate the destination model with the same parametrizations and wrappers used when the checkpoint was saved.
For spectral normalization, apply the same parametrization before loading.
For `AveragedModel`, load the wrapped module state or map the exact `module.` namespace deliberately.
Check missing and unexpected keys rather than hiding structural mismatches with a blanket permissive load.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Wrappers and parametrizations change checkpoint key topology; the destination model was structurally different even though its conceptual architecture was similar.
generalized_repairs.title: Match wrapper and parametrization topology before loading state
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when checkpoint keys differ systematically by `module.` or parametrization suffixes rather than by isolated missing layers.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Checkpoint or SWA averaging fails with `mean(): ... Got: Long`, commonly on BatchNorm `num_batches_tracked` or another non-floating state entry.
repair_steps: Inspect the dtype of each state-dictionary value before averaging.
Average only floating-point or complex tensors.
For integer or boolean buffers, copy a consistent value from one selected checkpoint instead of taking a mean.
Load the reconstructed state only after every key has the expected dtype and shape.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Model state dictionaries include non-trainable integer buffers, but the averaging loop treated every entry as a floating parameter.
generalized_repairs.title: Average only floating checkpoint tensors
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when SWA or manual checkpoint averaging succeeds for most keys but fails on a `Long` tensor.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `RuntimeError: grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs` at `loss.backward()` when mixup combines per-sample criterion outputs.
repair_steps: Inspect the criterion reduction and the shape returned by the mixup loss.
Combine the two target losses with `lam` while preserving per-sample semantics.
Apply `.mean()` after the weighted combination so the value passed to `backward()` is scalar.
Assert `loss.ndim == 0` before backpropagation.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The criterion produced one or more losses per sample, and the mixup wrapper returned that tensor without a final reduction.
generalized_repairs.title: Reduce mixup loss to a scalar before backward
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when forward computation succeeds but backward rejects a non-scalar loss.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `sklearn.metrics.log_loss` raises a class-count mismatch because a validation fold contains 90 or 98 classes while predictions contain all 99 probability columns.
repair_steps: Confirm labels are encoded contiguously from `0` through `n_classes-1`.
Call `log_loss` with `labels=np.arange(n_classes)`.
Keep prediction columns in that same encoded class order.
Do not drop probability columns merely because a particular fold lacks those classes.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: `log_loss` inferred its class universe from the fold’s `y_true`, which omitted classes still represented in the fixed-width prediction matrix.
generalized_repairs.title: Pass the full encoded class universe to log_loss
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when prediction width is correct but a fold omits one or more classes from `y_true`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A stratified holdout with `test_size=72` cannot cover 99 classes, or nested `StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5)` exceeds the smallest class membership.
repair_steps: Count members per class before selecting a split strategy.
For a holdout expected to contain every class, require at least one row per class on both sides; in the supplied failure, 72 validation rows cannot represent 99 classes.
Require `n_splits` not to exceed the minimum class count for stratified K-fold.
Reduce folds or enlarge the holdout only when those arithmetic constraints are satisfied.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The requested stratification geometry was mathematically impossible for the class counts and partition sizes.
generalized_repairs.title: Preflight class counts before stratified splitting
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use before constructing a stratified holdout or nested fold on a many-class, low-sample dataset.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: SMOTE raises `Expected n_neighbors <= n_samples_fit`, specifically `n_neighbors=6` with a class containing only 5 training samples when `k_neighbors=5`.
repair_steps: Compute the minimum post-split class count before constructing SMOTE.
Choose `k_neighbors <= min_class_count - 1`; the supplied repair uses `k_neighbors=1` when at least two samples exist.
If any class has fewer than two samples, do not apply ordinary SMOTE to that class.
Run oversampling only on the training partition.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: SMOTE internally requires the selected neighbors plus the sample itself, so `k_neighbors=5` requires at least six class members.
generalized_repairs.title: Bound SMOTE neighbors by the smallest training class
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when oversampling follows a split and rare classes may have fewer than six members.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: `BatchNorm1d` raises `Expected more than 1 value per channel when training`, with input such as `torch.Size([1, 256])` from a final partial training batch.
repair_steps: Check the remainder of training-set size divided by batch size.
Set `drop_last=True` on the training DataLoader when the remainder would produce a singleton batch.
Keep validation and test evaluation in `model.eval()` and do not discard their rows for this training-only condition.
Assert training batches contain at least two samples before calling a BatchNorm model.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: BatchNorm in training mode cannot estimate batch statistics from one sample, and the DataLoader emitted a singleton final batch.
generalized_repairs.title: Prevent singleton training batches for BatchNorm models
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when failure occurs only on the last training batch and the reported BatchNorm input begins with dimension one.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Cached image features have 704 rows while training indices address 712 rows because extraction used `drop_last=True` with batches of 16.
repair_steps: Use a dedicated deterministic extraction DataLoader with `drop_last=False`.
Disable shuffling or retain explicit sample IDs so output order is recoverable.
Assert extracted row count equals the source dataset count before caching.
Store IDs beside cached features and verify them before indexed training.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: A training-oriented loader policy silently discarded the incomplete extraction batch, breaking row alignment with labels and indices.
generalized_repairs.title: Never drop rows during deterministic feature extraction
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when an extracted or cached feature matrix is shorter than the dataset by one partial batch.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: CUDA initialization or shared-memory worker failure with `num_workers>0`, or `cannot pin 'torch.cuda.FloatTensor'` when CUDA tensors are supplied to a pinning DataLoader.
repair_steps: Keep dataset tensors on CPU and move each batch to the target device inside the training or inference loop.
Use `num_workers=0` in the constrained runtime when worker CUDA initialization or shared-memory errors occur.
Use `pin_memory` only for dense CPU tensors; otherwise set it to `False`.
Do not configure `persistent_workers` or `prefetch_factor` when no worker processes are used.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: CUDA tensors or CUDA-dependent work crossed DataLoader worker/pinning boundaries that support CPU-owned tensors and available shared memory only.
generalized_repairs.title: Keep DataLoader storage on CPU and device transfer in the loop
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when worker processes report CUDA initialization, bus errors, or pinning errors before the model forward pass.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A loader returns a singleton list/tuple, a label-bearing 4- or 5-item tuple, or a dictionary, but consumer code calls `.to()`/`.size()` on the container or unpacks the wrong arity.
repair_steps: Define the exact batch schema for training, validation, and test datasets.
Unpack singleton `TensorDataset` batches before calling tensor methods.
Allow prediction code to distinguish feature-only batches from batches that also include labels.
For dictionary batches, move each tensor value separately and obtain batch size from a designated tensor.
Do not index `batch[0]` when the DataLoader already returns a batched feature tensor rather than a tuple.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Dataset return types differed by phase, while shared consumer code assumed one fixed tensor/tuple representation.
generalized_repairs.title: Make loader batch structure explicit for every phase
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use for `list has no attribute to`, `dict has no attribute size`, or `too many/not enough values to unpack` failures.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Two feature streams are combined batchwise but one test loader uses batch size 32 and the paired CNN loader uses 16, producing a tensor mismatch at dimension zero.
repair_steps: Give synchronized loaders identical batch size, row order, shuffle policy, and final-batch policy.
Verify the two batch lengths before combining their tensors.
Prefer storing aligned modalities in one dataset when possible so one sampler controls both streams.
Retain sample IDs to verify alignment through the final partial batch.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Independently batched modalities no longer represented the same rows in the same batch, so fusion combined tensors with different leading dimensions.
generalized_repairs.title: Synchronize batch geometry across paired feature loaders
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when separately loaded modalities have matching total rows but fail only during batchwise fusion.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A model assumes three 64-column groups or another hardcoded layout, but preprocessing produces 439 total features, group widths 84/84/80, 237 rather than 231 columns, or 513 rather than the declared 512 image features.
repair_steps: After preprocessing, construct an explicit ordered layout containing each group’s start, end, and width.
Initialize every branch from the measured width in that layout rather than assuming 64 columns or divisibility by three.
Apply the same ordered transform and layout to train, validation, and test.
Assert every slice width and total width immediately before model construction and again in `forward()`.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Feature engineering, PCA, or concatenation changed widths and ordering, while model slicing and layer construction retained raw-schema constants.
generalized_repairs.title: Generate a feature-layout manifest after every transformation
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use for branch-level matrix multiplication failures after feature engineering or dimensionality reduction.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A concatenated tensor has width 1536 but the classifier expects 1024, width 2048 but the fusion layer expects 1024, or another `mat1 and mat2` mismatch whose input width equals the sum of multiple embeddings.
repair_steps: Record the output width of every concatenated operand.
Set the following `Linear.in_features` to the exact sum of those widths.
If a representation is unintentionally duplicated, remove that operand instead of merely enlarging the layer.
Assert the concatenated tensor’s last dimension before invoking the linear layer.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The architecture concatenated more representations than the downstream layer’s declared input width accounted for.
generalized_repairs.title: Set post-concatenation layers from the sum of operand widths
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when the runtime input width is an exact sum such as `1024+512=1536` or `1024+1024=2048`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Elementwise addition or `torch.stack` receives widths such as 384 versus 192 or 512 versus 256; or attention expects embedding dimension 384 while tokens have 128, or query/key dimensions differ 32 versus 128.
generalized_repairs.method_family: Common-latent projection and attention shape contracts
repair_steps: Before addition or stacking, project every participating modality to one shared latent width.
Configure `MultiheadAttention.embed_dim` to equal the token tensor’s final dimension.
Ensure query, key, and value head dimensions agree before `einsum` or attention scoring.
Use concatenation with a correctly sized downstream projection when equal-width elementwise fusion is not intended.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Fusion operators requiring equal dimensions were applied to modality outputs or attention tensors with incompatible latent widths.
generalized_repairs.title: Project modalities and attention tokens to compatible dimensions
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when failure occurs at `+`, `stack`, `MultiheadAttention`, or `einsum` rather than at raw feature slicing.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: A full SigLIP/SigLIP2 model is called with only `pixel_values` and raises `ValueError: You have to specify input_ids`.
repair_steps: Determine whether the task needs joint image-text inference or image-only embeddings.
For image-only extraction, call the model’s `vision_model` subcomponent with image inputs.
If joint inference is genuinely intended, supply the required text `input_ids` through the processor.
Do not call the full multimodal forward with only `pixel_values`.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The full SigLIP forward contract includes the text tower, while the code intended to use only the vision tower.
generalized_repairs.title: Use the SigLIP vision submodel for image-only embeddings
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when SigLIP receives valid images but explicitly demands `input_ids`.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Backbone loading fails because `{TORCH_HUB_DIR}` is literal, `hubconf.py` is missing or unreadable, a cache directory is unwritable, a model tag is unknown, or a remote weight download returns HTTP 403.
repair_steps: Resolve placeholders to real paths before calling `torch.hub.load`.
For local hub loading, verify `hubconf.py` exists and is readable.
Place writable caches outside read-only input directories.
Validate model identifiers against the installed library before requesting pretrained weights.
If the artifact is unavailable, fail or disable only the optional component; do not claim results from an unexecuted replacement.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: The code treated an unavailable, invalid, unreadable, or inaccessible model artifact as guaranteed runtime infrastructure.
generalized_repairs.title: Preflight model identifiers, hub paths, permissions, and access
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when failure occurs before feature extraction in `torch.hub`, `timm.create_model`, or cache-directory setup.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: OOF predictions for 179 rows are assigned to 712 training indices; fold arrays of 179 and 178 rows are added directly; or internal OOF predictions for 712 rows are blended against a separate 179-row holdout.
repair_steps: Allocate one full OOF matrix with one row per training sample.
Scatter each fold’s validation predictions into that matrix using `val_idx`, never `train_idx`.
Keep internal OOF, external holdout, and test predictions as distinct artifacts with row IDs and shapes.
When evaluating an external holdout, use predictions explicitly produced for that holdout, not internal OOF output.
Do not elementwise average validation arrays from folds with different row counts.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Prediction arrays from different row domains were treated as interchangeable because their class dimension matched, while their sample identities and lengths did not.
generalized_repairs.title: Track OOF, holdout, and test predictions by row provenance
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use for broadcasting, assignment, or ensemble failures where class width matches but sample counts differ.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Engineered skew, kurtosis, ratios, scaling, logits, or probabilities contain NaN/Inf; training begins with NaN loss, `log_loss` rejects NaN, or submission validation reports NaN probabilities.
repair_steps: Guard every denominator and undefined statistic during feature construction.
For deterministic engineered features, replace only documented undefined values with finite defaults after the guarded computation.
Assert finiteness after feature engineering, scaling, model output, softmax, and fold averaging.
If logits or probabilities are non-finite, stop and trace the producing model rather than silently ranking it.
For finite probabilities, enforce nonnegative values and renormalize each row before submission.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: Undefined statistics or numerically unstable model outputs propagated across stage boundaries without finite-value validation.
generalized_repairs.title: Validate finite features and probabilities at every boundary
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when NaN appears in the first epoch, metric computation, fold averaging, or submission assertions.

generalized_repairs.failure_pattern: Importing `skimage` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lazy_loader'`, preventing startup or optional morphology/LBP extraction.
repair_steps: Do not import the unavailable `skimage` dependency at module startup when its features are optional.
Remove the optional morphology branch or implement the required simple operation with available PIL/NumPy primitives.
Keep train and test feature construction identical after removing the dependency.
If class-column ordering is affected, continue to derive it from `sample_submission.csv`.
generalized_repairs.root_cause: An optional image feature path made the entire pipeline depend on an incomplete scikit-image installation.
generalized_repairs.title: Isolate optional skimage features from the core pipeline
generalized_repairs.when_to_use: Use when the supplied tabular pipeline is otherwise usable but `skimage` fails through its missing `lazy_loader` dependency.

coverage_risks: Many supplied entries are repeated observations across attempts; source IDs above are representative evidence sets rather than an exhaustive duplicate listing.
Most entries provide a diagnosed failure and proposed local repair, but not a recorded successful post-repair rerun. Treat unverified one-off repairs as candidates until reproduced.
Some failure narratives and repair rationales diverge. This distillation retains only directly evidenced exception/API/operand/shape relationships.
Library signatures are environment-specific; apply a family only after matching the exact callable and exception in the active runtime.

Lower-frequency mechanisms such as negative-stride arrays after flips, CUDA tensors passed to sklearn, processor attribute differences, and individual SciPy/NumPy helper availability remain outside the top 30 families.
do_not_generalize: Do not promote validation metrics, ensemble weights, backbones, feature strategies, pseudo-labeling, or model rankings from quarantined, protocol-biased, blocked, warning, or failed programs.

Do not generalize methods carrying `TRANSFORM_FIT_BEFORE_SPLIT`, `TRANSFORM_FIT_ON_HOLDOUT`, `GROUP_SPLIT_LEAKAGE`, `TEMPORAL_SPLIT_LEAKAGE`, `VALIDATION_REUSED_FOR_EARLY_STOPPING_AND_REPORT`, `REPORT_SET_REUSED_FOR_ENSEMBLE_SELECTION`, or `LLM_SELECTION_BIAS`.
Do not fit PCA, scalers, selectors, or ensemble weights on validation/report data merely to stabilize dimensions or remove an exception.
Do not use `strict=False`, zero-image fallbacks, NaN replacement, or model disabling as silent ways to conceal an unresolved structural failure.
Do not use `weights_only=False` for checkpoints that are not locally produced and trusted.
Do not treat observed constants such as 99 classes, 64 raw features per group, or a particular backbone input size as universal unless the active artifacts reproduce those preconditions.
Do not infer successful submission generation from a strong intermediate metric when the recorded process exited abnormally.
ranking_recommendations: Rank exact exception, API namespace, symbol, operand, and tensor-shape matches above broad category similarity.

Prefer families supported by repeated `positive_eligible` clean claims, especially checkpoint loading, XGBoost compatibility, class-universe metrics, feature-layout contracts, and DataLoader contracts.
Use quarantined or protocol-biased claims only as evidence for the isolated local runtime repair; exclude their model choices and metrics from ranking.
Before expensive execution, rank parse/import, schema, split-feasibility, row-count, shape, and finite-value preflights as mandatory gates.
Promote a repair to durable positive memory only after a post-repair run verifies the affected stage and preserves leakage-safe train/validation boundaries.
